source: OpenScore String Quartets (CC0-1.0), https://github.com/OpenScore/StringQuartets, branch main, fetched 2026-10-10
notes: Measure numbers are the printed bar numbers read by music21 (Measure.number). A movement that opens with an anacrusis numbers it 0 (Haydn Op.76/3 II, Op.20/2 I); otherwise numbering starts at 1. The pickup bar is a short Measure (paddingLeft > 0).

Every file here holds a WHOLE quartet: all movements in one .mxl, one continuous Part per instrument, with measure numbers restarting at each movement (0 or 1). OpenScore does also have per-movement files for a few works (e.g. Mozart K.464 is four .mxl files), but none are used here. movement_index is the 0-based movement within the file, found by measure-number resets.

Trap: score.measures(start, end) on the full file matches those numbers in EVERY movement (measures(1,2) returned 8 bars per part). extract.load_excerpt therefore selects by 0-based measure index: measure_index_range = [first, last] inclusive, into part.getElementsByClass('Measure'); the same index is valid for all four parts.

Split measures: a mid-bar double bar or repeat (e.g. each Emperor variation starts with a half-bar pickup) yields two Measure objects with the same number; the second carries numberSuffix 'X1', 'X2', ... Convention in extract.resolve_index_range: a duplicated start number begins at its LAST occurrence (the pickup), a duplicated end number stops at its FIRST occurrence (the closing half-bar). So 'm40-60' for Var. II = pickup half of m.40 through the first half of m.60.

music21's measures(..., indicesNotNumbers=True) end index is EXCLUSIVE, and it collects Clef/KeySignature at the Part level rather than in the first Measure; load_excerpt moves them into the first measure (pulling from context when missing) so every part's first measure has clef, key and time signature.

Pitches: string parts are non-transposing and no excerpt contains an ottava spanner, so written = sounding. part_ranges are sounding pitch (computed after toSoundingPitch()) and include chord tones and grace notes.

Grace notes appear (quarterLength 0, duration.isGrace) in the Dvorak Lento and Hensel Romanza; tempo words are TextExpressions, and MuseScore's hidden playback tempi come through as MetronomeMarks with auto-generated names (e.g. 'lento') that are not in the printed score.
Part names: the files name the parts 'Violin 1', 'Violin 2', 'Viola', 'Violoncello' (music21 part ids P1-P4, always in that order); the manifest uses 'Violin I', 'Violin II', 'Viola', 'Violoncello'.

MusicXML round trip (load_excerpt -> write('musicxml') -> parse) preserves part and note counts for all six excerpts, except one dotted-quarter tremolo note in Dvorak Op.96 I m.1 that music21 splits into a tied pair on export (456 -> 457 notes).

Fingered/measured tremolo: Dvorak Op.96 I mm.1-6 accompaniment is written as alternating F5/A5 values in Violin I and A4/F4 in Violin II (shimmer accompaniment), carried as TremoloSpanner/Tremolo marks; the written durations are not the played rhythm. Hensel Romanza mm.5 and 13 have tremolo marks in Violin II/Viola/Cello.
melody_map: entries may overlap when two parts are in dialogue (marked in 'note'); bars not covered by any entry have no single melodic line (intro or transition).
part_stats.notes counts note onsets (tied continuations excluded); chords counts music21 Chord objects (string double stops); chords_in_excerpt is their sum across parts.

excerpts.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
excerpts.why: Easy hero: Haydn's “Emperor” hymn, melody in Violin I over a clean four-part chorale accompaniment.

excerpts.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
excerpts.movement: II. Poco adagio; cantabile — Var. II
excerpts.why: Same hymn moved to the cello while Violin I plays a syncopated countermelody above it: a top-voice baseline picks the wrong line.

melody_map.note: hymn tune, octave below the Theme; Violin I countermelody sits above it

excerpts.title: String Quartet No.12 in F major, Op.96 (“American”)
excerpts.why: Pretty and clear, then a handoff: Violin I sings the theme, then the cello takes it over while Violin I drops to the repeated-note accompaniment on top.

melody_map.note: same theme an octave lower; Violin I is top voice but plays accompaniment

excerpts.title: String Quartet No.12 in F major, Op.96 (“American”)
excerpts.why: The famous viola opening: the theme starts in the viola under violin tremolo, moves to Violin I, then trades between cello and Violin I and cascades up through all four parts.

melody_map.note: theme head on beats 1-2, answered by Violin I on beats 3-4
rising arpeggio motif; mm.15-16 are transitional tremolo/arpeggio texture
motif; leads into the tutti restatement at m.21

excerpts.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:32, Op.20 No.2
excerpts.why: Cello leads in its tenor register above Violin II and viola while Violin I is silent, then Violin I takes over, then Violin II (doubled by viola) carries the line under a Violin I pedal.

melody_map.note: tenor register, above Violin II; Violin I rests mm.1-6
enters on the last eighth of m.6
doubled a third below by Viola; Violin I holds a G5 pedal on top

excerpts.title: String Quartet in E-flat major
excerpts.why: Fanny Hensel's Romanza: Violin I states the theme, the viola echoes a phrase, then the cello restates the theme in its high tenor register under a Violin I countermelody.

melody_map.note: echoes Violin I's m.9 figure a fifth lower
theme an octave below the opening, up to D5; Violin I countermelody above
